facts.text: In August the turn toward the east-face basin comes just after the first switchback above Source Lake, marked by a cairn; a faint path climbs the dry waterfall gully, then trees lead to the talus field below the face.
Start in the obvious chimney-crack at the middle of the face; protection is scarce, with the first piece about 60 ft up and little on the second pitch, so bring a full rack.
No anchors mark pitch ends below the rappel slings at the top, so choose belay stances at flakes and ledges yourself.

Going down the south gully, skip the first slung gully and the single sling on a boulder; head for the trees below, where four 60 m rappels reach the base, and watch for rockfall at the last station tucked behind an overhang.
A cairned, well-worn path runs from the basin back to the Source Lake trail and is gentler than the waterfall gully.
